newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine sees $300-900 mln int'l bond issues in '97.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine sees $300-900 mln int'l bond issues in '97.

text.p: Ukraine wants to raise between $300 and $900 million by tapping international bond markets this year to partially finance the 1997 deficit, the central bank chief said on Wednesday.

"The deficit would be covered in part by raising $300 to $900 million on the international market through Eurobonds or Samurai bonds," National Bank of Ukraine Chairman Viktor Yushchenko told a business meeting.
Ukraine is expected to issue its first bonds denominated in a foreign currency this year, and Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko said previously the bonds could be issued next month.

Yushchenko said the deficit, contained in a late budget which parliament is expected to debate and pass this month, would be 5.8 billion hryvnias, or four percent of gross domestic product using Western calculations.

He said most of the deficit would be covered by foreign bonds and sales of Treasury bills, and the rest would be covered by the International Monetary Fund, expected to give Ukraine a three-year credit of $2.5 to $3 billion once the tough budget is approved.

Yushchenko added that 1997 would be the first year when the central bank would not pay for the deficit by issuing direct credits to the government, a practice which in the past sent inflation skyrocketing.
